newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco - 49ers deal to cap stadium costs.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco - 49ers deal to cap stadium costs.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and the National Football League 49ers are finalizing an agreement to cap the city's investment in a proposed $535 million stadium, according to a report Monday.

The agreement, which would have the legal weight of a contract, would firm up the football team's financial obligations before the proposed stadium project goes to voters on June 3, the San Francisco Chronicle newspaper reported.
The team, which wants to build the new stadium and retail complex to replace aging 3Com Park, hopes the agreement will convince voters to support the project, the Chronicle said.
The Chronicle reported that the agreement would:
* Set a $100 million cap on the city's investment in the stadium and require the team to put up $4 in advance for every $1 the city puts into the deal.
* Clarify that any cost overruns would be paid by the team.
* Clarify that the team would cover all infrastructure costs and all expenses for improving roadways.
* Require that the city pay for half of most stadium maintenance costs.
